name: Do high elevation and dry Colorado climates affect interior log stains?

mainEntity.name: Do high elevation and dry Colorado climates affect interior log stains?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Colorado communities like Parker, Centennial, and foothills neighborhoods, indoor log care must account for low indoor humidity and strong high-altitude sunlight. Winter heating combined with naturally dry mountain air pulls moisture out of interior timbers, widening check cracks and drying out older clear coats. South- and west-facing windows also let in intense UV rays that bleach indoor wood unevenly. When refinishing logs in these areas, choosing an interior formula with mild UV protection and sealing log checks against dust helps prevent excessive wood drying and keeps interior timbers looking rich year-round.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes. Low regional humidity accelerates timber drying and log checking, while high-altitude UV through large windows can fade south-facing interior logs prematurely.
